notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text begins with the matching title No Personality Change Following Unemployment: A Registered Replication of Boyce, Wood, Daly, and Sedikides (2015), names Timo Gnambs and Barbara Stiglbauer, and contains methods, results, Table 6 on printed page 44, references and a supplement. It identifies itself as an accepted Journal of Research in Personality manuscript with final DOI 10.1016/j.jrp.2019.06.009. This supports identity as a primary report of the referenced replication; the supplied OSF preprint DOI is not printed in the text, so exact preprint-version correspondence is not independently established. No PDF path was supplied; no rendering performed. Table 6 prints Buadj (unbalanced) and Badj (balanced) versions. Page 20 discusses Buadj for the direct replication and pages 21–22 discuss the balanced extension; the assigned description/locator does not explicitly select a version. Preserve both candidates rather than assign the target by numeric agreement. Parameters other than intercept and variances are standardized with respect to the trait at the first measurement occasion, so these are not unstandardized b values. No metric or time-unit conversion was made. No analytic N is assigned because N is not an unfinished field. Candidate openness change regressed on unemployment at T2: Table 6 Buadj = -0.36; Badj = -0.27. Neither candidate slope coefficient has an asterisk; the table supplies only the significance-marker rule * p < .05 and does not print an exact p or an explicit individual p inequality for these slope tests. Absence of an asterisk is retained as a marker observation, not converted to a numerical p bound. The broad description also leaves baseline versus change unresolved: the Unemployed at T2 row under Openness prints baseline/intercept candidates Buadj = 0.80 (asterisk; p < .05), Badj = 0.58 (no asterisk). These must not be mixed with the Slope x Unemployed at T2 change coefficients. Unassigned fields are placeholders only.
